citations.excerpt: It was in this context that the Philippine Independent Church was born in 1902, out of the aspiration of the Filipinos for genuine independence, democracy and abundant life.
Under the theological leadership of Bishop Gregorio Aglipay, the IFI adopted a Unitarian stance, but after his death in 1941 it returned to a more Catholic position

facts.value: A church that, partly through the appeal of nationalism, drew some two million former Roman Catholics. In intercommunion with the Philippine Episcopal Church since 1961.

citations.excerpt: Partly because of the appeal of nationalism, the church drew some two million former Roman Catholics into its membership.
entered in 1961 into inter-communion with the Philippine Episcopal Church with which it now shares a seminary.

facts.value_before_verify: A Filipino national church that drew about two million former Roman Catholics. It returned to a Catholic position after 1941 and has been in intercommunion with the Philippine Episcopal Church since 1961.
